issues.title: Define composition of permission and capacity evidence
issues.author: thibmeu
issues.body:
An origin may need both an OAuth access token granting permission and a MOLE presentation proving capacity on the same request. The current header-based schemes both use `Authorization`, which carries one credentials value (RFC 9110, Section 11.6.2). Multiple `WWW-Authenticate` challenges offer alternatives; they do not signal that all must be satisfied.

For example, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ..., Mole ...` does not define how a client supplies both credentials or learns that both are required. MOLE's current HTTP transport also selects one presentation per request, leaving stacked workload and user budgets unresolved.

Define or reference a way to carry these credentials together and signal cumulative requirements, coordinating any transport changes with MOLE. Until then, the draft should describe these combinations as unresolved.

Raised in the review of PR #8: https://github.com/thibmeu/draft-capacity-management/pull/8#discussion_r4525546009

It expands the musings I put together and, with the help of Claude, provides a more thorough exploration of the deployment topologies. I made an attempt at reframing the core position of the draft too, moving away from rate limiting and towards the balance of attribution and private authentication.
